title: Epithelial tissue
summary: Sheets of tightly joined cells that line surfaces and form glands.

layers.basics: Epithelia cover your skin and line your gut, lungs and vessels. They are barriers that also absorb and secrete.
layers.deeper: Classified by cell layers (simple vs stratified) and shapes (squamous, cuboidal, columnar). They sit on a basement membrane and have no blood vessels.
layers.expert: Polarized cells joined by tight junctions, adherens junctions, desmosomes; apical and basolateral domains with distinct transporters; high turnover and stem-cell renewal.

did_you_know: Epithelial cells are the origin of about 85-90% of cancers (carcinomas).

title: Loose connective tissue
summary: A flexible packing tissue with fibers and cells in a gel-like matrix.

layers.basics: It fills spaces between organs and holds structures in place.
layers.deeper: Fibroblasts make collagen and elastin fibers in a ground substance of hydrated proteoglycans.
layers.expert: Areolar tissue is rich in fibroblasts, mast cells and macrophages; extracellular matrix composition determines mechanics.

did_you_know: Collagen is the most abundant protein in the human body.

title: Dense connective tissue
summary: Tough, fiber-packed tissue forming tendons, ligaments and capsules.

layers.basics: Very strong and rope-like tissue that links muscle to bone and bone to bone.
layers.deeper: Dense regular tissue has parallel collagen fibers (tendon); dense irregular has woven fibers (dermis).
layers.expert: Type I collagen fibrils bundled into fascicles; sparse fibroblasts (tenocytes); poor blood supply slows healing.

did_you_know: Tendons can store and return a significant part of the energy of a running stride.

title: Adipose tissue
summary: Fat tissue that stores energy and insulates.

layers.basics: Fat cells store extra energy as oil droplets and also cushion organs.
layers.deeper: White fat stores energy, brown fat makes heat, and fat also releases hormones such as leptin.
layers.expert: Adipocytes ≈ 70-120 µm; adipokines (leptin, adiponectin); beige adipocytes can express UCP1; typical body fat ≈ 15-30% in adults.

did_you_know: Brown fat, once thought only in infants, is also found in adults.

title: Cartilage
summary: Firm, flexible tissue found in joints, nose, ears and airways.

layers.basics: Cartilage is smoother and bendier than bone, and cushions joints.
layers.deeper: Chondrocytes in lacunae make a matrix rich in collagen II and proteoglycans, without blood vessels.
layers.expert: Hyaline, elastic and fibrocartilage types; avascular so repair is slow; aggrecan holds water giving compressive stiffness.

did_you_know: Your nose and ears are mostly cartilage and keep growing slightly through life.

title: Bone tissue
summary: Mineralized connective tissue that is hard yet living.

layers.basics: Bone is a living material, mostly collagen strengthened with calcium phosphate crystals.
layers.deeper: Cells within bone sense strain and direct remodeling, and blood vessels run through it.
layers.expert: About 65% mineral (hydroxyapatite), ≈ 25% organic (mostly collagen I) and ≈ 10% water by weight; osteon structure; turnover of ≈ 10% of the skeleton per year.

did_you_know: Most of your adult skeleton is replaced over about a decade.

title: Blood tissue
summary: A fluid connective tissue: cells suspended in plasma.

layers.basics: Blood is a tissue with floating cells in liquid.
layers.deeper: Cells include red cells, white cells and platelets; plasma carries proteins and solutes.
layers.expert: Hematopoiesis from HSCs; erythrocytes ≈ 4.5-5.5×10^12/L, leukocytes ≈ 4-11×10^9/L, platelets ≈ 150-400×10^9/L.

did_you_know: Red blood cells outnumber white cells about 700 to 1.

title: Skeletal muscle tissue
summary: Striped muscle tissue under voluntary control.

layers.basics: Muscles are bundles of long fibers that shorten when told to.
layers.deeper: Each muscle fiber is a giant multinucleated cell packed with striped contractile units.
layers.expert: Fibers bundled into fascicles with endomysium, perimysium, epimysium; satellite cells repair; motor-unit organization.

did_you_know: A muscle fiber can have hundreds of nuclei in one cell.

title: Cardiac muscle tissue
summary: Striated, involuntary muscle of the heart with branching cells.

layers.basics: The heart muscle never rests and cannot tire.
layers.deeper: Cells are joined end to end at intercalated discs, so electrical signals spread.
layers.expert: Gap junctions (connexin 43) enable syncytium-like conduction; desmosomes bear force; ≈ 25-35% of volume is mitochondria.

did_you_know: Heart muscle cells turn over very slowly, around 1% per year in young adults.

title: Smooth muscle tissue
summary: Unstriped involuntary muscle in vessel walls and organs.

layers.basics: Smooth muscle squeezes slowly without conscious control in the gut, vessels and bladder.
layers.deeper: Spindle-shaped cells with one nucleus; contractions are slow and sustained.
layers.expert: Contraction via Ca2+-calmodulin-MLCK phosphorylation of myosin light chain; latch state conserves ATP.

did_you_know: Uterine smooth muscle cells grow in length about tenfold during pregnancy.

title: Nervous tissue
summary: Tissue of neurons and supporting glial cells.

layers.basics: Neurons send signals; glial cells feed, insulate and protect them.
layers.deeper: Gray matter is cell-body rich and white matter holds myelinated fibers.
layers.expert: Neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, microglia (CNS); Schwann cells (PNS); glia:neuron ratio is ≈ 1:1 overall in the human brain.

did_you_know: The old '10 glia for each neuron' idea has been revised to roughly one to one.

title: Simple squamous epithelium
summary: A single layer of flat cells for fast exchange.

layers.basics: One thin layer of flat cells lines air sacs and blood vessels, letting gases pass easily.
layers.deeper: Found in alveoli (type I cells), capillary endothelium and mesothelium.
layers.expert: Thickness ≈ 0.1-0.5 µm in the alveolar wall; allows passive diffusion.

did_you_know: The alveolar wall that gases cross is far thinner than a human hair, about 1/100 the width.

title: Simple columnar epithelium
summary: A single layer of tall cells for absorption and secretion.

layers.basics: Tall cells line your intestines and absorb nutrients.
layers.deeper: Often has microvilli and goblet cells that secrete mucus.
layers.expert: Tight junctions between enterocytes separate lumen from internal milieu; brush border enzymes.

did_you_know: Goblet cells produce about a liter of mucus a day in the gut.

title: Stratified squamous epithelium
summary: Many layers of cells that resist wear, like skin.

layers.basics: Layered flat cells tough enough for the skin, mouth and esophagus.
layers.deeper: Keratinized in skin, non-keratinized in mouth and esophagus.
layers.expert: Basal stem cells renew the layers; differentiation moves cells to the surface.

did_you_know: The inside of your cheek replaces itself in about a week.

title: Transitional epithelium (urothelium)
summary: A stretchy multi-layer lining of the bladder and ureters.

layers.basics: This lining can stretch when the bladder fills.
layers.deeper: Umbrella cells flatten as the bladder expands.
layers.expert: Uroplakin plaques and tight junctions form a highly impermeable barrier to urine.

facts: one of the tightest in the body
did_you_know: It is among the least permeable epithelia in the body.
